intro.title: useSyncExternalStore
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple counter component that displays a value from an external store. You will learn how to use the React hook `useSyncExternalStore` to subscribe to and read data from an external state source, like a Redux store or a custom store, ensuring your component stays in sync with changes. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and the `useSyncExternalStore` hook for managing external state. This lesson will help you understand how to connect React components to state that lives outside of React's own state management, using a straightforward example suitable for beginners.
intro.usecase: useSyncExternalStore is essential for integrating React components with external state management libraries like Redux, Zustand, or custom stores. In real applications, you'll use it to keep UI components like dashboards, data tables, or real-time monitoring panels synchronized with external data sources. For example, a financial dashboard displaying live stock prices needs to stay updated with an external market data feed without causing unnecessary re-renders. This hook ensures your React components efficiently subscribe to and display the latest external state changes, making it crucial for building responsive, data-driven interfaces that rely on non-React state systems.
